entries.content_plain:
Introduction

 Asa succeeds his father Abijah, reigns piously, and has peace for ten years, 2Chr 14:1 . He makes a great reformation in Judah, and builds cities of defense, 2Chr 14:2-7 . His military strength, 2Chr 14:8 . He is attacked by Zerah the Ethiopian, with an immense army; Asa cries to the Lord, attacks the Ethiopians, and gives them a total overthrow, 2Chr 14:9-12 . He takes several of their cities, their cattle, etc., and returns to Jerusalem, laden with spoils, 2Chr 14:13-15 . 

 Verse 1 

 The land was quiet ten years - Calmet thinks these years should be counted from the fifth to the fifteenth of Asa's reign.

entries.content_osis: <hi type="bold">Verse 2</hi> <div eID="gen14215" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen14216" type="x-p"/> Did that which was good - He attended to what the law required relative to the worship of God. He was no idolater, though, morally speaking, he was not exempt from faults, <reference osisRef="1Kgs.15.14">1Kgs 15:14</reference>. He suppressed idolatry universally, and encouraged the people to worship the true God: see <reference osisRef="2Chr.14.3-2Chr.14.5">2Chr 14:3-5</reference>.

entries.content_osis: <hi type="bold">Verse 15</hi> <div eID="gen14224" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen14225" type="x-p"/> Tents of cattle - Those which had carried the baggage of the great army, and which they had left in such places as abounded with pasture. Perhaps sheepfolds, enclosures for camels, mules, etc., may also be intended. The discomfiture was great, because God fought for the people; and the spoil was immense, because the multitude was prodigious, indeed almost incredible, a million of men in one place is almost too much for the mind to conceive, but there may be some mistake in the numerals: it is evident from the whole account that the number was vast and the spoil great.  <chapter eID="2Chr.14"/> <div eID="gen14225" type="x-p"/>
